open_points.subject: INV-18 ownership
open_points.text:
| INV-01, INV-02, INV-18 | `source_folder` |
- whether a photo was placed or published;
open_points.question: How can `source_folder` own the part of INV-18 stating that a conflict copy is not placed while it is expressly forbidden to own whether a photo was placed; does `source_folder` own only conflict-name eligibility, does `photo_delivery` own the placement guarantee, or is the prohibition meant to have an exception?
options: Split INV-18: `source_folder` owns exclusion from observations and source reads, while `photo_delivery` owns refusal of placement
Make `photo_delivery` the owner of the complete invariant and depend on `source_folder` for ignored-name classification
Keep `source_folder` as owner and state that eligibility for placement is not ownership of whether placement occurred
open_points.default_guess: Split the responsibility explicitly: `source_folder` owns conflict-copy detection and exclusion from eligible source reads; `photo_delivery` owns the resulting placement refusal.

open_points.subject: conflict-copy exclusion during placement
open_points.text:
- INV-18: a Syncthing conflict copy is neither reported by a scan nor placed.
- reading the bytes of one source file without following a link;
observe_source_files
read_source_bytes
open_points.question: Which `source_folder` capability structurally guarantees the placement half of INV-18, including a file whose name changes after observation: must `read_source_bytes` revalidate the ignored-name rule, must `observe_source_files` return an opaque observation that can be read safely, or must `photo_delivery` know and repeat the conflict-name rule; and which direct dependency symbols must `photo_delivery` import?
options: `read_source_bytes` revalidates that the selected path is still non-ignored before returning bytes
`observe_source_files` returns an opaque source handle and `read_source_bytes` validates that same observation without exposing the naming rule
`photo_delivery` imports or duplicates the ignored-name predicate and checks again before placement
open_points.default_guess: Keep the rule encapsulated in `source_folder`: return an opaque observation from `observe_source_files`, require it for `read_source_bytes`, and have that read reject a now-ignored conflict-copy name.
